findings: Defines unit, intervention and information clock before SCM/SWIG semantics and graph construction. Separation, adjustment and front-door derivations distinguish the kernel extracted by identification from an observational conditional.
Recursive ID/IDC traces retain joint nonidentification versus conditional rescue; observational-equivalence bounds and selection/mediation restrictions retain their substantive interpretation.
Derives the residual moment, 2SLS/GMM and complier functional with its weights; an observationally equivalent completion proves why the population ATE is not identified.

Weak relevance, invalid exclusion and support failure remain different failures. Gaussian Anderson–Rubin inversion, disconnected sets, nuisance-product errors and control-rank recovery carry explicit assumptions.
The control-function support counterexample and nonlinear inverse equation connect structural identification to the later functional analysis without treating a learned residual as sufficient.
Derives the ATE gradient and remainder; orthogonality, double robustness and fold-specific empirical control remain distinct requirements.
Local conditional-effect estimation, average effects, targeting and policy selection retain their different rates, information sets and evaluation obligations.

Separates injective function identification from target-functional identification and regularity through operator range and closure; the singular-sequence calculation is not promoted to a full estimated-operator rate theorem.
Proxy bridge existence, uniqueness, completeness and support retain separate roles. The signed treatment-bridge example shows why clipping changes the estimand.

extraction_limit: Mathematical glyph extraction can omit an overbar; surrounding prose in the operator argument explicitly names closure. This is not evidence of a PDF typography defect and no visual claim follows.
conclusion: No consequential new defect established in these bounded complete rendered-text contexts. Earlier scholarship objections now have developed arguments; independent sufficiency and visual acceptance remain open.
